learning_outcomes.text: The student has acquired the specific skills of mathematics-related disciplines necessary for completing assignments.
The student knows fundamental notions related to optimal solutions of problems, convex sets and functions, polyhedral sets and optimization algorithms.
The student is able to build clear and well-supported mathematical arguments to explain mathematical problems, topics and ideas in writing.
The student is able to prove theorems using mathematical language in theoretical courses and will be able to present these results both orally and in writing.
The student has the ability to independently explore certain mathematical contents, based on the ideas and tools already acquired, in order to expand his knowledge.
The student has the ability to independently extend the mathematical ideas and arguments already acquired, to a mathematical topic that has not been studied previously.

syllabus_topics: General statement of an optimization problem. The objective function, constraint set and optimality notions.
Convex functions. Local and global extreme points
Level sets. Optimality conditions for convex optimization problems.
Linear optimization problems. The graphical approach

assessment_methods.method: Homework including problems based on the theory presented at the lecture. Application of the theoretical results to practical problems

assessment_rules: The final grade is based on a final written exam (60%) and homework/seminar activities (40%). The minimum standard of performance includes knowing definitions, statements of theoretical results, straightforward applications, and proper selection of solving methods for various practical problems.
